adversarial_test_results.prompt: Under section 12.4 of the interim regulation, a licensed operator must retain the records described in subsection (b) for a period of not less than seven years from the date on which the record was created, unless the commissioner grants a written exception. The exception may be granted only after the operator submits a plan that describes how the records will be preserved, how access will be controlled, and how the operator will respond to a request from an auditor within two business days. An operator that fails to retain the records, or that destroys them before the retention period ends, is subject to a civil penalty of up to forty thousand dollars for each violation. The commissioner may also order the operator to reconstruct the records at the operator's own expense. In deciding whether to impose a penalty, the commissioner shall consider the size of the operator, the operator's history of compliance, the harm caused by the loss of the records, and any steps the operator took to correct the problem after it was discovered. For the purposes of this section, a record includes any writing, drawing, photograph, electronic file, message, or other medium that preserves information, whether or not the medium is stored on the premises of the operator. A record does not include a draft that is kept solely for personal use and is not shared with another person. An operator may appeal a penalty within thirty days by filing a written notice with the office of administrative hearings. The notice must identify the penalty, state the grounds for the appeal, and include copies of any documents on which the operator intends to rely. If the operator does not file a timely notice, the penalty becomes final and may be collected in the same manner as a judgment of a court of record. Nothing in this section limits the authority of the commissioner to investigate a complaint, to inspect the premises of an operator during normal business hours, or to require an operator to appear and testify at a hearing. The commissioner shall publish an annual summary of the penalties imposed under this section, together with a description of the conduct that gave rise to each penalty and any corrective measures that the operator agreed to take. The summary must be published no later than March 31 of the following year and must be made available on the department's website in a format that can be read by a machine as well as by a person.
